findings.criterion: 2 and 3 — scanned-pass verification and camera check-in correctness
findings.issue: Flow persists above the nested check-in routes, but passSeq is a ref owned by CheckInCapture. A camera plate can route an in-flight lookup to Confirm; Back to edit then remounts CheckInCapture with a new sequence ref while the old request closure can still update the persistent flow. If pass B resolves before older pass A, both are current in their independent refs and A can overwrite B. The pure harness uses one latestSeq closure and does not model this remount. A newer wrong-site QR also returns before incrementing passSeq, so it fails to supersede an older request.
findings.consequence: After explicitly scanning a newer pass, the attendant can redeem an older guest's pass, associating the vehicle/session with the wrong host and leaving the intended pass active.
findings.correction: Move the monotonically increasing lookup generation and optional abort controller into Flow so they survive child-route remounts. Invalidate the prior generation at the start of every non-empty scan before local wrong-site rejection, and clear pending state for a current local rejection. Add a regression that starts A, navigates Confirm to edit, starts B in the remounted capture, resolves B then A, and proves B remains attached; also prove a newer wrong-site scan invalidates A and that rendered submission redeems only B.

findings.criterion: 1 — resident can actually share a scannable QR pass
findings.issue: This iteration again supplied no rendered/component/browser execution for the file-share, text-share, clipboard/download, public guest-page, and rendered QR paths. Pure helper tests do not establish that the actual button emits a usable artifact, a deployed direct /pass fragment URL renders, or its QR reaches lookup/redeem.
findings.consequence: The acceptance-critical resident-to-guest Share workflow remains unverified across its reachable browser capability branches.
findings.correction: Add and run rendered/browser coverage for all three share capability branches; inspect the emitted artifact, open the guest URL directly, decode or scan its rendered QR, complete lookup/redeem, and record browser and mobile viewport.

findings.criterion: 2 plus accessibility — pass prepopulate, focus, edit, and submit in context
findings.issue: The recorded tests exercise extracted state helpers rather than React, routing, focus, or network submission. No executed UI path proves that a signed hinted pass fills the visible editable plate field, focuses and announces acceptance, survives edit/remove/replace, redeems instead of opening a walk-in, and persists the correct association.
findings.consequence: The required scan-to-prepopulated-form-to-verification-to-submit workflow is not established in the actual UI.
findings.correction: Add and run a component/browser integration story covering those observations and the lookup lifecycle race, then assert the persisted session/pass/plate association.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera scanning fills check-in and checkout plate fields
findings.issue: The fake-camera check-in story was explicitly not run, and no checkout fake-camera story exists. Pure decoder and ALPR tests do not execute getUserMedia through the React callbacks, controlled plate fields, routing, or checkout matching.
findings.consequence: Actual camera-to-field behavior for both required workflows remains unverified in context.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 fake-camera check-in story; add and run checkout coverage that opens a session, scans its plate, asserts the checkout field and correct match without manual entry, and records browser, fixture/model, viewport, and result.

findings.issue: The new API test now proves a non-default configured value reaches all three currency-formatted 12-hour notices and the event, but no rendered execution edits the Settings field, saves through PATCH /v1/pass-policy, reloads, and observes persistence. The existing unrun browser story only reads the MXN default.
findings.consequence: Execution evidence still does not prove administrators can persist the required per-tenant policy from the UI or that unauthorized roles cannot edit it.
findings.correction: Add and run a browser test that changes the amount as an authorized administrator, saves, reloads, and confirms the same major-unit value; also verify a role without settings.edit cannot edit or save it.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 plus mobile/responsive authorization — Admin CRUD and Super Admin cross-property operations
findings.issue: The relevant browser stories were again not run. They remain desktop-only; the Super Admin story switches property but performs no edit/delete there, and no rendered test proves a regular administrator cannot read or mutate the second property.
findings.consequence: The user-facing mobile CRUD workflows and cross-property authorization boundary required by criteria 6 and 7 remain unverified.
findings.correction: Run the existing stories; add representative person/site/unit/slot CRUD at a narrow mobile viewport, perform edit/delete after a Super Admin switches to a second property, and assert a regular administrator is denied that property's reads and mutations.
